You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From fbf65674a471d12e43f4050086969f417e00891f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nick Owens <mischief@coreos.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jul 2016 15:39:02 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] net: add client arch and fix user class/terminator

send client arch in bootp requests, for now BIOS and x64/aarch64 EFI is
supported.

fix a bug introduced in 4d5d7be005bb5c15c07472461b528dea65a58cc6 where
user class was encoded improperly, although this didn't seem to have any
detrimental effects.

properly insert an option terminator.
---
 grub-core/net/bootp.c | 22 +++++++++++++++++++++-
 1 file changed, 21 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/grub-core/net/bootp.c b/grub-core/net/bootp.c
index f211c911d..a40163a6f 100644
--- a/grub-core/net/bootp.c
+++ b/grub-core/net/bootp.c
@@ -25,11 +25,21 @@
 #include <grub/net/udp.h>
 #include <grub/datetime.h>
 
+#if !defined(GRUB_MACHINE_EFI) && (defined(__i386__) || defined(__x86_64__))
+#define GRUB_NET_BOOTP_ARCH 0x0000
+#elif defined(GRUB_MACHINE_EFI) && defined(__x86_64__)
+#define GRUB_NET_BOOTP_ARCH 0x0007
+#elif defined(GRUB_MACHINE_EFI) && defined(__aarch64__)
+#define GRUB_NET_BOOTP_ARCH 0x000B
+#else
+#error "unknown bootp architecture"
+#endif
+
 static grub_uint8_t dhcp_option_header[] = {GRUB_NET_BOOTP_RFC1048_MAGIC_0,
 					    GRUB_NET_BOOTP_RFC1048_MAGIC_1,
 					    GRUB_NET_BOOTP_RFC1048_MAGIC_2,
 					    GRUB_NET_BOOTP_RFC1048_MAGIC_3};
-static grub_uint8_t grub_userclass[] = {0x4D, 0x05, 'G', 'R', 'U', 'B', '2'};
+static grub_uint8_t grub_userclass[] = {0x4D, 0x06, 0x05, 'G', 'R', 'U', 'B', '2'};
 static grub_uint8_t grub_dhcpdiscover[] = {0x35, 0x01, 0x01};
 static grub_uint8_t grub_dhcptime[] = {0x33, 0x04, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0e, 0x10};
 
@@ -546,6 +556,16 @@ grub_cmd_bootp (struct grub_command *cmd __attribute__ ((unused)),
 	  offset += sizeof(grub_userclass);
 	  grub_memcpy (offset, grub_dhcptime, sizeof(grub_dhcptime));
 
+	  /* insert Client System Architecture (option 93) */
+	  offset += sizeof(grub_dhcptime);
+	  offset[0] = 93;
+	  offset[1] = 2;
+	  offset[2] = (GRUB_NET_BOOTP_ARCH >> 8);
+	  offset[3] = (GRUB_NET_BOOTP_ARCH & 0xFF);
+
+	  /* option terminator */
+	  offset[4] = 255;
+
 	  grub_netbuff_push (nb, sizeof (*udph));
 
 	  udph = (struct udphdr *) nb->data;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an improper encoding of the user class in the BOOTP request, specifically in the size of the user class array. The original code incorrectly defined the size of the `grub_userclass` array, which led to an incorrect representation of the user class option in the BOOTP packet. Additionally, the patch introduced the insertion of a client system architecture option (option 93) and ensured that a proper option terminator (255) was included, which was missing in the previous implementation.

    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    Code statements:
    <text1>

    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an improper encoding of the user class in the BOOTP request, specifically in the size of the user class array. The original code incorrectly defined the size of the `grub_userclass` array, which led to an incorrect representation of the user class option in the BOOTP packet. Additionally, the patch introduced the insertion of a client system architecture option (option 93) and ensured that a proper option terminator (255) was included, which was missing in the previous implementation.
